newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian-Romanian ferry link hit by raised taxes.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian-Romanian ferry link hit by raised taxes.

text.p: Traffic through the ferry link between the Bulgarian port of Oryahovo and the Romanian port of Beket across the Danube river border has dropped sharply after Romania raised road taxes, officials said on Monday.

The executive director of the Oryahovo Ferry Complex Mihail Mihailov said the Romanian road administration had surprisingly increased road taxes from their town of Craiova to Beket to $258 from $150 for trucks over 32 tonnes and busses over 13 tonnes.

"This tax...has a negative effect on the international motor traffic which provoked immediate strong protests by speditors," Mihailov said in letter faxed to Reuters. He did not say how much the traffic has declined.
Mihailov said a considerable part of the road traffic had been diverted via Yugoslavia and other links where road taxes are cheaper.
The Oryahovo authorities have said their ferry link, launched last year, provided the shortest route between Turkey and western Europe.
